fields.description:
## Context / Problem
`_pai_structured` creates fresh Agent runs for prompted-output recovery, so output attempts can reset the request budget and retry history is assembled outside Pydantic (`structured_run.py:87-178`). The approved RP-01 contract instead uses the Pydantic output-policy adapter [rebar:grazeable-preferred-bumblebee] (S1, now landed: `src/rebar/llm/pai_output.py` — review against `--ref HEAD`, which carries the stacked S1 change) in one Agent operation while preserving every authoritative input and stored response.

## Approach
Replace the manual structured-output attempt scheduler with one Pydantic `Agent` run that composes the S1 adapter (`pai_output.output_function` as `output_type=TextOutput(fn)`) with two new seams from a focused `src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py` helper:

1. **Wire-context projection — a pydantic-ai `history_processors` `HistoryProcessor`.** The concrete seam is the Agent-level `history_processors=[proc]` (`pydantic_ai._history_processor.HistoryProcessor`): a callable run before each model request that returns a COPY for the wire without mutating stored state, so `result.all_messages()` keeps the full history regardless of what the wire copy omits. It puts the complete failed `ModelResponse` on the retry wire ONLY when every viable candidate has a known window and a token count proving `input_tokens + effective_max_tokens <= window`; else it omits that response WHOLE (never partially; unknown window/count → omit). Authoritative input (system/user/tool) that cannot fit fails closed with a typed fit/context error — never shortened.

2. **Truncation reclassification — a concision-aware operation guard.** For this operation ONLY, `pai_retry` supplies its own `after_model_request` capability (attached INSTEAD OF `pai_output.guard_capability()`, whose terminal-truncation contract stays UNCHANGED for every other caller until S5 cutover). It co-locates the reclassification: (a) it resolves the reason through the SAME shared classifier (`structured.check_stop_reason`, which normalizes both `finish_reason` and the raw `provider_details` two-layer shape), and when that reason is the truncation subset (`length`/`max_tokens`) raises, before parsing, `pydantic_ai.ModelRetry("Make your response as concise as possible while fulfilling the prompt and output format requirements.")` — a bounded, in-run retry; (b) otherwise it delegates to the SAME S1 logic — call `structured.check_response(response)`, re-raise a terminal `UnretryableOutputError` (refusal/`content_filter`; one call, no retry), and translate a retryable `StructuredOutputError` (transient `error`) into `ModelRetry` so pydantic-ai retries rather than aborts (only the truncation branch differs from S1's guard). The shared `structured.py` tables (`_UNRETRYABLE_STOP_REASONS`, `check_stop_reason`) are NOT modified.

3. **One shared request budget, one shared retry counter.** `structured_run.py`'s `build_usage_limits` sets the operation-wide `UsageLimits.request_limit` = base request allowance (`ceil(eff_max_iter/2)`) PLUS the configured output-retry allowance, computed once with NO per-attempt reset. Crucially the value it RETURNS as `req_limit` (consumed by telemetry and by `completion_banking.iteration_limit_for`) stays the BARE base `ceil(eff_max_iter/2)`; the output allowance is an addend only inside the constructed `UsageLimits`, so the `2×B` inverse is preserved exactly. Output-size (concision) and parse/validation retries draw from the SAME counter — `structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES` (=2), lowered only by `req.structured_retry_limit` — not a separate budget. A single truncation spends one unit; on exhaustion pydantic-ai raises `UnexpectedModelBehavior`, which the operation translates into a rebar-typed exhaustion error (`UnretryableOutputError`).

The concision `ModelRetry` is in-run, so it never reaches `FallbackModel.fallback_on` — output-size retry structurally cannot trigger fallback.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py` — new: (a) the `HistoryProcessor` wire-context projection (fit decision + non-mutating whole-response include/omit) and (b) the concision-aware operation guard (`length`/`max_tokens` → bounded concision `ModelRetry`; delegate refusal/`content_filter`/`error` to `structured.check_response`). A module docstring records the combined-allowance derivation. No provider selection, usage projection, or persistence.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — replace the manual `_pai_structured` attempt scheduling with one Agent operation; extend `build_usage_limits` to derive the combined operation-wide `request_limit` (base + output allowance) without resetting counters (this is where `req_limit` is computed, not `agent_call.py`).
- `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` — thread the two new seams and `retries={"output": allowance}` into `build_agent_kwargs` (wiring only; it does not compute the allowance).
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — compose the helper without growing past the 800-line cap.
- `tests/unit/test_structured_run.py`, `test_runner_pydantic_budget.py`, `test_pydantic_ai_runner.py`, and `test_settings_builders_seam.py` (its `limits.request_limit` assertion moves 5→base+allowance) — operation, history, and limit contracts.

**Cross-directory consumers of the `ceil(x/2)` request-budget shape** (symbol-graph sweep of `build_usage_limits`, not hand-enumerated): `workflow/completion_banking.py:iteration_limit_for` inverts `ceil(eff_max_iter/2)` as `2×B`, and `completion_banking.py:plan_recovery_pool` independently applies `ceil(floor/2)` to the verify-step floor. Both are left exact because `build_usage_limits` keeps RETURNING the bare base `req_limit` (the allowance lives only inside the constructed `UsageLimits`). `usage_log.py`/`runner.py` only receive the built `request_limit` as an argument. A source-census test pins the returned `req_limit == ceil(eff_max_iter/2)` while `UsageLimits.request_limit == base+allowance`, and enumerates these two formula encodings as the authoritative set.

## Testing
- Boundary: complete response fits (on wire) / does not fit (omitted whole, `all_messages()` complete) / count unknown (omitted) / authoritative input cannot fit (typed error, no shortening).
- Limit: tool turn + output retry succeeds at the derived allowance and fails one below it; repeated output-size failure exhausts the shared allowance.
- Terminal: refusal/content-filter is one call, no output retry, no fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Invalid-then-valid structured output completes through one Pydantic Agent run and reports exactly two Pydantic requests under one shared `UsageLimits`; verified by focused real-`FunctionModel` tests.
- [ ] A complete 5,000-character failed response is present on the retry wire only when the full request plus output reserve provably fits (`input_tokens + effective_max_tokens <= window` for every viable candidate); verified by a complete-fit test.
- [ ] When it does not fit — or window/token count is unknown — zero characters from that response are on the retry wire, while `result.all_messages()` retains all 5,000; verified by omit and unknown-count tests.
- [ ] Authoritative-input overflow raises the typed fit/context failure without shortening system, user, or tool content; verified by an oversize-input failure test.
- [ ] `length`/`max_tokens` consumes at most the configured output-retry allowance (shared with parse/validation retries; not a separate counter) and sends exactly "Make your response as concise as possible while fulfilling the prompt and output format requirements."; verified by a success case and an exhaustion case.
- [ ] Refusal/content-filter remains terminal after one model call and activates neither output retry nor provider fallback (structurally: an in-run `ModelRetry` never reaches the `fallback_on` predicate); verified by call-count and candidate-count assertions.
- [ ] The combined request allowance is documented in the `pai_retry.py` module docstring as raiseable through a normal reviewed follow-up, and no per-attempt reset path remains in the new scheduler; verified by that docstring plus a source-census and budget test.
